title: Tabbouleh
subtitle: Lebanese herb salad with bulgur wheat and tomato
excerpt: The great Lebanese herb salad: mountains of flat-leaf parsley and mint with a small amount of fine bulgur wheat, tomato, spring onion, and a sharp lemon dressing. More herb than grain.

recipe.sourceNotes: Tabbouleh (also spelled tabbouli or tabouleh) is one of the most widely known dishes of Lebanese and Levantine cuisine, eaten throughout the Middle East, the Arab diaspora, and increasingly worldwide. In Lebanon, where the dish originated, tabbouleh is considered a herb salad first and a grain salad second: the proportion of parsley to bulgur wheat is very high, often five to one or more. The westernised version, which uses a much higher ratio of bulgur to herbs, is quite different in character. Traditional Lebanese tabbouleh uses very fine bulgur wheat (number 1 or 00 grade) that is simply soaked in the lemon juice rather than cooked, allowing the grains to swell. The herb must be flat-leaf parsley, not curly: curly parsley produces a bitter, coarser result. The salad wilts quickly and should be dressed and served immediately.

content.text: The parsley must be dried thoroughly after washing or the salad will be watery. Spread it on a clean tea towel and pat dry before chopping. Chop the parsley finely but not so finely that it becomes paste: a sharp knife and a chopping board are better than a food processor. The bulgur wheat is soaked rather than cooked: cover with the lemon juice, stir, and leave for 20 minutes. It will absorb the juice and swell. Salt the tomato cubes and drain them before adding to prevent the salad from becoming watery.

items.preparation: washed, dried, and very finely chopped
ripe; finely diced; salted and drained

content.text: Combine the bulgur wheat and lemon juice in a bowl. Stir to coat. Leave to soak for 20 minutes until the grains are tender and have absorbed most of the juice.
Dice and salt the tomatoes in a separate bowl, leave for 10 minutes, then drain. Add the finely chopped parsley, mint, and spring onion to the bulgur. Fold in the drained tomatoes.
Dress with olive oil, season with salt and pepper. Taste: tabbouleh should be very sharp with lemon and generously seasoned. Serve immediately.
